meta.titre: Reported Speech: moving direct speech into the past
meta.sous_theme: Statements, questions and commands in indirect speech

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A mother in Bamenda comes home and tells her husband what the headmaster said at the parents' meeting. She does not repeat every word she heard. She retells it: the headmaster said that the school would close early, and he asked everybody to collect the report cards. This retelling is reported speech. Examiners test it with sentences to be changed or chosen, and the points they check are tense, pronouns, time words and word order.

items: Direct speech is placed in quotation marks and gives the exact words spoken.
The main tenses are the present, past and perfect forms.
A pronoun such as I or you changes with the speaker.

sections.titre: Turning direct speech into reported speech
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Direct and reported speech

Direct speech gives the speaker's exact words in quotation marks. Reported (indirect) speech tells what was said without quoting: *Ngwa said that he was tired.* When the reporting verb is in the past (*said*, *asked*, *told*), the tenses usually move one step back and several other words change.

### Backshift of tenses

| Direct speech | Reported speech |
|---|---|
| present simple: *I live here.* | past simple: *She said that she lived there.* |
| present continuous: *I am reading.* | past continuous: *He said that he was reading.* |
| present perfect: *I have finished.* | past perfect: *He said that he had finished.* |
| past simple: *I bought a book.* | past perfect: *She said that she had bought a book.* |
| will, can, may | would, could, might |

Modal verbs that are already past in form (*would*, *could*, *should*, *might*) stay unchanged. No backshift is needed when the reporting verb is in the present (*He says that he is tired*) or when the statement is a general truth (*The teacher said that the Earth moves round the Sun*).

### Changes of pronouns, time and place

Pronouns change with the point of view: *I* becomes *he* or *she*, *my* becomes *his* or *her*, *we* becomes *they*. Expressions of time and place change when the report is made at a different time or place.

| Direct | Reported |
|---|---|
| now | then |
| today | that day |
| yesterday | the day before / the previous day |
| tomorrow | the next day / the following day |
| last week | the week before |
| ago | before |
| here | there |
| this / these | that / those |

### The four sentence types

1. **Statements:** *said (that)* or *told + person + that*. Do not write *said me*.
2. **Yes/no questions:** *asked* + *if* or *whether*, with statement word order, no auxiliary *do*, and a full stop at the end.
3. **Wh- questions:** keep the question word, use statement word order, no auxiliary *do*, and a full stop.
4. **Commands and requests:** *told / asked / ordered + person + to-infinitive*; for a negative command use *not to*.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the direct speech is a statement
variantes.contenu_markdown: Change the tense one step back, change the pronouns and the time words, and join with *that*. *"We are studying for the GCE," they said* becomes *They said that they were studying for the GCE.* *"I will call you tomorrow," she told me* becomes *She told me that she would call me the next day.*

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the direct speech is a question
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use *asked* and drop the question mark. For a yes/no question add *if* or *whether*: *"Do you like football?" she asked me* becomes *She asked me if I liked football.* For a wh- question keep the question word: *"Where do you live?" he asked me* becomes *He asked me where I lived.* A question with *can* becomes one with *could*: *"Can you help me?" Amina asked him* becomes *Amina asked him if he could help her.*

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the direct speech gives an order, a request or a warning
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use a reporting verb with an object and the to-infinitive. *"Close the window," the teacher said to us* becomes *The teacher told us to close the window.* *"Don't be late," my mother said* becomes *My mother told me not to be late.* There is no *that* and no change of tense.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Report the following speech.

*Mr Fon said to the class, "Where did you leave your textbooks yesterday? I want them here tomorrow."*

etapes.justification: There are two sentences: a wh- question and a statement. The report will need two reporting verbs.
The question needs *asked* with the people addressed, and the statement can follow with *added that*.

etapes.action: Backshift the tenses and change the pronouns.
etapes.justification: *Did you leave* becomes *they had left*, *your* becomes *their*, and *I want* becomes *he wanted*.
etapes.resultat_markdown: they had left their textbooks / he wanted them

etapes.action: Change the time and place words.
etapes.justification: *Yesterday* becomes *the day before*, *tomorrow* becomes *the next day*, and *here* becomes *there*.
etapes.resultat_markdown: the day before / the next day / there

etapes.action: Fix the word order and the punctuation.
etapes.justification: A reported question has statement order and no question mark. The whole report ends with a full stop.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The report is: **Mr Fon asked the class where they had left their textbooks the day before and added that he wanted them there the next day.**

items.erreur_markdown: *He asked me where did I live.* (wrong)
items.pourquoi_faux: A reported question takes statement word order, without the auxiliary *did*.
items.correction_markdown: Write **He asked me where I lived.**

items.erreur_markdown: Reporting *"The patient is very weak," said the doctor* as *The doctor said that the patient is very weak.* (wrong in a transformation exercise)
items.pourquoi_faux: After a past reporting verb the tense moves back. A transformation item expects the backshifted form.
items.correction_markdown: Write **The doctor said that the patient was very weak.**

items.erreur_markdown: Keeping the time word in a report made on a later day: *She said that she had met him yesterday.* (wrong in a transformation exercise)
items.pourquoi_faux: The time word must change when the report is made at a different time.
items.correction_markdown: Write **She said that she had met him the day before.**

items.pourquoi_faux: A person after the reporting verb needs *told*, and a command takes the to-infinitive.
A reported question is a statement in form, so it ends with a full stop.
items.correction_markdown: Write **She asked if I was ready.**

items.enonce_markdown:
Change into reported speech.

(a) "I am tired," said Kamga.

(b) "We live in Bafoussam," they said.

(c) "She has gone to market," my aunt said.

(d) "I can swim," the boy said.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Kamga said that he was tired.**

(b) **They said that they lived in Bafoussam.**

(c) **My aunt said that she had gone to market.**

(d) **The boy said that he could swim.**

items.enonce_markdown:
Change into reported speech.

(a) "Why are you crying?" the nurse asked the child.

(b) "Have you seen my keys?" Tabe asked me.

(c) "Open your books," the teacher said to the pupils.

(d) "Don't touch the wires," the engineer warned them.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **The nurse asked the child why he (or she) was crying.**

(b) **Tabe asked me if (or whether) I had seen his keys.**

(c) **The teacher told the pupils to open their books.**

(d) **The engineer warned them not to touch the wires.**

items.enonce_markdown:
Change into reported speech.

(a) Mary said to Paul, "I shall visit my uncle in Kumba next week, and I hope you will come with me."

(b) "Did the bus leave before the rain started?" the old man asked.

(c) "Don't forget to lock the door when you leave tomorrow," my father said to me.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Mary told Paul that she would visit her uncle in Kumba the following week and that she hoped he would go (or come) with her.** (*I shall* becomes *she would*, *next week* becomes *the following week*)

(b) **The old man asked whether (or if) the bus had left before the rain had started.** (*Started* is also accepted after *before*.)

(c) **My father told me not to forget to lock the door when I left the next day.**

items_markdown: After a past reporting verb the tenses move one step back: present to past, past to past perfect, will to would.
Change the pronouns with the point of view and change the time and place words: now to then, yesterday to the day before, here to there.
A reported question has statement word order, no do, and a full stop; yes/no questions take if or whether.
Commands and requests are reported with told or asked + person + to-infinitive, and not to for a negative command.
No backshift is needed for a general truth or when the reporting verb is in the present.
